text:
maria: quick heads up — AcmePayments is seeing flapping healthchecks from our edge in eu-central. They say the source IPs for our healthchecks rotate and their firewall/proxy is blocking.
kevin: which IPs are they seeing?
maria: they pasted two: 18.214.33.12 and 3.120.99.45 — but they say it changes every few hours.
jess: those look like ephemeral ELB NAT IPs. We're using cloud LB in front of edge nodes; health probes originate from the LB's public-facing NAT, which can vary.
maria: customer wants a single static IP to allowlist. not possible for hosted right now, they asked for guidance.
adi: short answer — ask them to allow a /22 for our eu-central egress pool or allow the healthcheck DNS (healthcheck.eu-central.redwood-inference.net) outbound. long answer below.
kevin: what about hairpin/NAT issues? they said when they put a proxy in front of their app we see 407s in our logs. sample from their side:```HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required
Proxy-Agent: squid/3.5.12
```
jess: common. If a customer terminates TLS at a proxy that isn't doing CONNECT for health probes, the LB will see SNI mismatch or proxy auth required. We require transparent TLS passthrough for our health checks (we expect a TCP handshake and client hello to the target host).
maria: pasted their curl run:```curl -v https://app.acmepayments.internal/health -x http://corp-proxy:3128``` -> returns 407.
adi: two practical options for customers: 1) allow outbound CONNECT to our healthcheck FQDN on 443 (preferred), or 2) allow the whole egress CIDR we publish for the region.
tony: we should publish an official, regularly-updated egress CIDR list (not per-IP). healthcheck-bot: scheduled task created: publish egress-cidrs per region to docs every 4h.
healthcheck-bot: note: ephemeral IPs may still change during infra scale events; CIDRs are more stable than single IPs.
kevin: also remind customers about hairpin/hop limits — if they SNAT inside an outbound proxy, source port preservation can break long-lived connections. not relevant to short probes but good to call out.
jess: recommended copy for support reply: "For hosted health checks we recommend allowing outbound TCP to healthcheck.<region>.redwood-inference.net:443 or allowing the eu-central CIDR range: 18.214.32.0/22 and 3.120.96.0/22 (these are regional NAT blocks). Avoid allowlisting single IPs — they rotate with scaling and failover."
maria: can we share those CIDRs publicly in docs now?
tony: yes but mark them as best-effort and link to a page we update automatically. I can hook the bot to regenerate when we change LB pools.
adi: for customers that require fixed egress, note Dedicated customers can request static NAT egress. add that to the reply.
kevin: extra note on proxy TLS inspection: if customer's proxy does MITM/TLS intercept, healthchecks will fail unless they present a cert that matches our hostname. so either disable inspection for that route or allow a passthrough.
jess: small troubleshooting snippet for support to run if customer reports 407:```# from customer's network
openssl s_client -connect healthcheck.eu-central.redwood-inference.net:443 -servername healthcheck.eu-central.redwood-inference.net
# if this times out or returns proxy headers, their proxy is intercepting or blocking CONNECT```
maria: thanks — I'll send this to the customer. tagging @kevin for follow-up if they escalate to Dedicated. :thumbsup:
kevin: lgtm. I'll add a note to the eu-central runbook about LB healthcheck NAT behavior and link the published CIDR page. :eyes:
healthcheck-bot: created ticket INF-4271 to add CIDR publish automation and a small blurb in onboarding docs.
